geometry_selection.conclusion: Ranking geometries on history does not predict their holdout result.

interpretation: Exit geometry cannot be chosen from this data: development ranking and holdout result correlate at -0.13, and the geometry selected on development failed to beat the shipped one on holdout. The entry signal's alpha over a random entry is by contrast robust to geometry - between 0.587% and 0.992% per episode, significant for all 24 grid entries after Holm correction. On the shipped geometry the holdout random arm returned -0.653% per episode while the signal arm returned -0.003%, so the signal converted a losing environment into a flat one without producing profit. The strategy is structurally long-only and the median instrument fell 17.7% over the window, which is where the alpha is going.
limitations: A single holdout window; its regime may not represent others.
Random control draws entries uniformly, a weaker benchmark than matched exposure.
Perpetual funding and maker fill risk remain unmodelled.
No short side exists in the codebase, so market-neutral capture was not testable.
